text.p: These are some of the leading stories in Israeli newspapers on Sunday.
Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- Three Israeli soldiers killed in Lebanon.
- U.S. Secretary of State Madeleine Albright won't visit until stalemate ends.
- Three paratroopers killed in Lebanon; high-ranking officer: We've reached a deadlock, the only solution is political.

- U.S. Middle East envoy Dennis Ross told Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat: Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu's government will complete its term. Netanyahu told this to cabinet ministers and guests because, based on polls he initiated, he would beat Labour party's Ehud Barak.
- Histadrut to declare a general work dispute today.
- Shas party leader Aryeh Deri acting to reappoint Yaacov Neeman as justice minister.
- Arafat writes to U.S. President Bill Clinton: Get involved to save the peace.
- Fear of greater Hizbollah activity against Israeli army.
- Israel plans to invite heads of leading multi-national companies to economic conference to mark 50 years of statehood in 1998.
